editorial:
If you love watching a tough cop punch his way through bad guys, this movie delivers big time. 'Monster Cop' Ma Seok-do is back, and this time he's chasing an illegal online gambling empire run by a dangerous former special forces soldier named Baek and a smart tech CEO named Chang. The story moves fast, mixing brutal fight scenes with funny moments that keep things light. Ma is the kind of hero who solves problems with his fists first and questions later, and that energy carries the whole film. You'll feel the stakes rise as the gambling ring's reach grows, and Ma's decision to team up with an unlikely ally named Jang adds a fun twist to the chase. The action is loud, the humor lands well, and the pacing rarely slows down.

The standout here is the action choreography and Don Lee's commanding presence. Every fight feels heavy and satisfying, and the supporting cast keeps up nicely. On the downside, the plot can feel a bit familiar if you've seen the earlier Roundup films, and some side characters don't get much development. Still, if you want a fun, no-nonsense action movie for a weekend night, this is a great pick.
endingExplained: In the final act, Ma Seok-do tracks Baek and Chang to their hideout. After a brutal showdown, Ma defeats Baek in hand-to-hand combat and arrests him. Chang tries to escape but is caught thanks to Jang's help. The gambling empire is shut down, and Ma walks away with another win, setting up future adventures. The movie ends on a light, triumphant note with Ma back on the beat.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves action-packed crime thrillers with a tough hero and big laughs.
